go_guidance: Expose a small synchronous API with New Store SignID VerifyID and VerifyIDByPrefix
rationale: HMAC signing and verification are CPU-local operations and do not need context unless a future key provider is introduced

go_guidance: Include both plain Store structs and an ergonomic Builder API in the first Go release
rationale: Plain structs keep configuration transparent and testable while the builder gives users a safer guided setup path

go_guidance: Return Result[T] values instead of Go errors for expected signing and verification failures
rationale: Preserves the TypeScript railway-style contract and keeps callers branching on status

go_guidance: Return (*Crypt error) from New when store configuration is invalid
rationale: Configuration errors are programmer/setup failures and should be caught before runtime signing

go_guidance: Return failure Result values for invalid payloads passed to SignID or decoded from tokens
rationale: Payload failures are part of normal data handling and map to stable protocol steps

go_guidance: Represent scope values as []string and normalize single string values into one-element slices during JSON decoding
rationale: Go cannot express string|string[] directly and slice equality should be value-based

go_guidance: Compare expected scope values by normalized string-slice contents rather than reference identity
rationale: The TypeScript implementation currently uses Object.is which makes array scope portability ambiguous

go_guidance: Convert Expiration to time.Duration and reject non-positive values or unknown units
rationale: Go callers should get deterministic validation before token creation

go_guidance: Use a maintained JWT or JOSE library and explicitly restrict accepted methods to HS256 HS384 and HS512
rationale: Prevents algorithm confusion and preserves the strength mapping

go_guidance: Use strings.LastIndexByte(fullToken ':') to split prefix from JWT
rationale: Matches the final-colon rule and supports prefixes that contain colons

go_guidance: Verify JWT algorithm signature and expiration before accepting claims validating payload shape or checking scope
rationale: This intentionally favors Go trust boundaries over the TypeScript decode-before-verify order

go_guidance: Use verify-id/decode-token only when a JWT cannot be decoded or parsed before claims validation
rationale: Separates malformed token structure from verified claims that fail payload validation

go_guidance: Try the current secret first and only try AltSecret after current verification fails
rationale: Preserves rotation behavior and makes finalMessage meaningful when both secrets fail

go_guidance: Return IDPayload without Exp on successful verification
rationale: Keeps JWT protocol claims out of application payloads

go_guidance: Keep step strings byte-for-byte stable across Go and TypeScript
rationale: Allows cross-language tests and caller logic to rely on deterministic failures

go_guidance: Add fixed-secret fixed-time contract tests before implementing release behavior
rationale: Prevents accidental divergence in token syntax algorithm mapping and error results
